reason: The text explicitly names several regular human characters: Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Reuel/Raguel (רְעוּאֵל, the priest of Midian and father), Zipporah (צִפֹּרָה, one of his daughters), and Gershom (גֵּרְשֹׁם, the son born to Moses and Zipporah). All of these are presented as ordinary people engaged in mundane human activities—drawing water, herding sheep, eating bread, and having children. None are divine or supernatural beings.
